paragraphs: A typical day revolves around listening, negotiating, and deciding. In the morning, an arbitrator presides over an employment dispute hearing and lets each side explain its position. In the afternoon, private caucuses test limits and identify common ground. In the evening, the arbitrator decides whether to pursue settlement or move into adjudication and draft the required documents.

paragraphs: A 5/10 score places dispute resolution in the moderate AI exposure range for knowledge work. AI can substantially improve document drafting, research, and recordkeeping, while mediation and adjudication remain person-to-person work. The score also signals that arbitrators who use AI can handle more cases, while career paths based only on desk research will narrow.

Moderate exposure is not a crisis. Court caseloads are growing, court-connected mediation is expanding, and demand for professional mediators is rising. Give document and research work to AI, then invest the saved time in industry expertise such as construction, finance, or intellectual property and in a strong mediation reputation. That combination improves negotiating power.

A law degree provides the foundation for this path, supported by psychology or an industry field such as finance or engineering. Pass the legal qualification exam, then build practical experience in legal practice or an in-house role. Arbitration and mediation reward experience over time, so do not expect immediate seniority.

Develop deep expertise in a field such as employment, commercial, family, or intellectual property disputes. Earn arbitrator credentials or join a mediation roster. Use AI for document and legal research, while focusing personal effort on mediation technique and industry knowledge. Professional reputation generates case referrals.

Lawyers, in-house counsel, and HR professionals have useful experience for this transition, especially in employment and family mediation. Start in a mediator role at an arbitration organization to build case volume. In interviews, explain disputes you successfully resolved rather than listing credentials.

Arbitration and mediation organizations should create a clear mediator → arbitrator → presiding arbitrator progression, make case-based compensation transparent, and provide AI drafting and research tools. This lets specialists spend their time on mediation and decisions.

The greatest career risk is not AI but dependence on public trust and case referrals. Decisions and settlements rely on professional reputation, and a single biased action can destroy credibility. Entry-level mediation has many cases but low pay, while high-end commercial arbitration pays well but has formidable entry barriers.
